To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the notations used in visual modeling are specificational and that (ii) the specificational format can be represented in the arrow-diagrams logic.

(1) the arrow logic of visual notations is a universal logic of visual modeling; (2) the arrow logic is a logic of diagram predicates and diagram operations; (3) the arrow logic provides a unified view of the notational diversity; (4) the arrow logic can be used as an effective tool for the analysis, synthesis, and design of visual notations; (5) the arrow logic offers a new approach to the problem of notational standardization.
the notational diversity in the visual modeling domain is due to the diversity of visualizing the same basic specificative format and the format is best approached by the arrow diagram logic.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) What is the logic of graphic notations, (2) What are the common features of various visual modeling languages, and (3) What is the universal logic underlying various visual modeling languages?
the question of the “what” vs. “how” of visual modeling: the “what” is the basic format of visual specifications and the “how” is the diversity of notational systems used to visualize this format.
the question of what is the common logical core of various notational systems, and what is its role in the process of visual modeling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the notational diversity of visual modeling can be explained by the diversity of diagram predicates and their operations, and that the diversity can be well approached from a unified perspective of the arrow-diagram logical format.
there is no one single logic for the whole of visual modeling but that there is a single logic for the core of visual modeling, namely for the specificational part of visual modeling.
the arrow logic of graphic notations is the logic of the arrow diagrams of specifications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the notational diversity is a matter of the diversity of diagram predicates and the diversity of diagram operations.
the arrow-diagram approach to visual notations is an attempt to develop a universal language for visual specifications.
we have shown how to represent the notational diversity of various visual modeling languages in the framework of arrow logic of graphic notations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notational diversity of visual modeling can be explained by a universal logic of visual specifications.
the diversity of notations can be explained by the diversity of diagram predicates.
a visual notation can be viewed as an arrow diagram, and the arrow logic of a notation can be explicated by means of a formal diagram calculus.
